prompt: Rust vs Go for backend services: performance, concurrency, and ecosystem trade-offs
report:
# Rust vs Go for Backend Services

## Performance
Rust generally outperforms Go on CPU-bound workloads because it has no garbage collection pause and compiles to tighter machine code [S1][S2]. Go's garbage collection keeps latency predictable for most services but adds tail-latency jitter under heavy allocation [S3].

## Concurrency
Go's goroutine model and channels make concurrent code simple and cheap to spawn [S3][S4]. Rust offers fearless concurrency enforced at compile time through its ownership and borrow checker, eliminating data races but with a steeper learning curve [S1][S5].

## Ecosystem
Go has a more mature standard library for HTTP services and faster compile times [S4]. Rust's async ecosystem (tokio) is powerful but more fragmented [S2][S6].

## Verdict
Choose Go for fast iteration and simple concurrency via goroutine pools; choose Rust when ownership-guaranteed safety and raw performance justify the ramp-up [S5].
